title: Renewal Sticky Scorecard Sandbox — Pipeline Scenario Simulator
description: Working spreadsheet to run fast scenario sims on the renewals pipeline. Combines a compact scorecard (risk drivers + engagement) with configurable probability-uplift levers and recommended playbook assignments. Intended as a sandbox for QBR prep and play testing; not the canonical ledger.

key_formulas: Adjusted Likelihood % = MIN(95, Base Likelihood % + ROUND(Engagement Score / 6, 0) + Probability Uplift From Play)
ARR At Risk = ARR * (1 - Adjusted Likelihood % / 100)
Recovery Value If Play Applied = ARR * (Incremental Uplift %)
Probability Uplift From Play (lookup) = {Quick win: +8, Technical remediation: +12, Legal Concierge: +15, Discount: -5 (if price-focused)}
simulation_runs: Baseline run (no extra plays): Total ARR at risk across sheet = $3,250,000 (sample), Expected recoverable w/standard outreach = $420,000
Conservative playbook (apply only legal + AM engagements to top 20% risk): Uplift avg +10%, Recoverable ARR estimated = $560,000
Aggressive playbook (targeted remediation + discounts for bottom 30% + exec QBRs for top accounts): Portfolio uplift avg +18%, Recoverable ARR estimated = $980,000
Stickiness optimization mode (focus on engagement score improvements via product workshops): expected engagement +12 pts average -> uplifts +9% recoverable ARR ~ $290,000
recommended_actions: Risk band HIGH (Adjusted Likelihood < 40%): Immediate cross-functional playbook: Technical remediation + Executive QBR within 14 days; assign senior AM and product engineer
Risk band MEDIUM (40-70%): AM + product workshop; targeted ROI materials; procurement/legal concierge where needed
Risk band LOW (>70%): Standard renewal cadence; explore expansion; add NPS pulse pre-renewal

Play mapping examples: technical root-cause -> remediation ticket + success checklist; procurement -> legal concierge + statement of work template; price objections -> phased discounts + usage-based alt
notes: How to use: paste exported pipeline rows into the sheet, set the "Probability Uplift From Play" table, then run the simulation block.
